title: The weak-tuple prism preserves repetitions and satisfies the augmented boundary identity
statement:
Use the integer-degree differential convention of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology], so a differential in degree $n$ has target degree $n-1$. Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $P,Q$ be finite partially ordered sets, possibly empty, and let $f,g:P\to Q$ be monotone maps satisfying $f(x)\leq g(x)$ for every $x\in P$. For $S=P,Q$ and $n\geq0$, let $W_n(S;R)$ be the free $R$-module on weakly increasing tuples $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, including tuples with repetitions as distinct basis elements. Put $W_{-1}(S;R)=R[\varnothing]$ and $W_n(S;R)=0$ for $n<-1$. Let $d_n$ be alternating vertex deletion for $n\geq0$ (so $d_0[x]=[\varnothing]$) and zero for $n<0$. Let $D_n(S;R)$ be the span of repeated tuples for $n\geq1$, and zero for $n\leq0$. For $u=f,g$, define $W(u)_n$ by entrywise image in nonnegative degrees, by the identity of $R$ in degree $-1$, and by zero below $-1$. For $n\geq0$ and a weakly increasing tuple $x$, put
$$T_i(x)=(f(x_0),\ldots,f(x_i),g(x_i),\ldots,g(x_n))\quad(0\leq i\leq n),\qquad H_n[x]=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i[T_i(x)],$$
and put $H_n=0$ for $n<0$. Every $T_i(x)$ is weakly increasing, so this specifies an $R$-linear map $H_n:W_n(P;R)\to W_{n+1}(Q;R)$. It satisfies $H_n(D_n(P;R))\subseteq D_{n+1}(Q;R)$ for every integer $n$, and the following equality of $R$-linear maps holds in every integer degree:
$$d_{n+1}H_n+H_{n-1}d_n=W(g)_n-W(f)_n.$$
In particular these assertions include degree zero when $f(x)=g(x)$, degree $-1$ with the fixed empty generator, all lower degrees, and empty $P$ or $Q$.

proof.text: For $n\geq0$, the $f$ segment and the $g$ segment of $T_i(x)$ are weakly increasing by monotonicity; the junction is $f(x_i)\leq g(x_i)$. Thus every summand is a basis tuple and extends linearly. If $x_a=x_b$ with $a<b$, weak increase gives $x_a=x_{a+1}$ by antisymmetry. Fix such an adjacent pair $x_a=x_{a+1}$.

source.place: Tag 019S, lemma-homotopy-s-N; preceding equation-homotopy-to-homotopy and its four-sum cancellation, lines 4739–4820. Agent adaptation to weak poset tuples, positive prism sign, repetitions, and augmentation.

proof.text: If $i\leq a$, both $g(x_a)$ and $g(x_{a+1})$ occur in $T_i(x)$; if $i\geq a+1$, both $f(x_a)$ and $f(x_{a+1})$ occur. In either case $T_i(x)$ is repeated. Hence every summand of $H_n$ on every generator of $D_n$ belongs to $D_{n+1}$, and linearity proves the inclusion for $n\geq1$. For $n\leq0$ its source $D_n$ is zero.

proof.text: Now let $n\geq1$ and denote deletion of position $j$ by $\partial_j$. Expand $dH[x]=\sum_{i=0}^n\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^{i+j}[\partial_jT_i(x)]$. Also $Hd[x]=\sum_{k=0}^n\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}(-1)^{k+r}[T_r(\partial_kx)]$. For $j<i$, deleting the $f(x_j)$ entry gives $\partial_jT_i(x)=T_{i-1}(\partial_jx)$. Its coefficient $(-1)^{i+j}$ cancels the coefficient $(-1)^{j+i-1}$ of precisely this term in $Hd[x]$.

source.place: Tag 019S, lemma-homotopy-s-N; preceding equation-homotopy-to-homotopy and its four-sum cancellation, lines 4739–4820. Agent adaptation to weak poset tuples, positive prism sign, repetitions, and augmentation.

proof.text: For $j>i+1$, deleting the $g(x_{j-1})$ entry gives $\partial_jT_i(x)=T_i(\partial_{j-1}x)$. The coefficients in $dH$ and $Hd$ are $(-1)^{i+j}$ and $(-1)^{j-1+i}$, which cancel. These pairings exhaust $Hd$: for its deletion index $k$ and pivot $r$, use $(i,j)=(r+1,k)$ if $k\leq r$, and $(i,j)=(r,k+1)$ if $k>r$. In the first case $j<i$; in the second $j>i+1$, with $0\leq i\leq n$ in both. These are inverse reindexings, even if different terms happen to be equal tuples.

source.place: Tag 019S, lemma-homotopy-s-N; preceding equation-homotopy-to-homotopy and its four-sum cancellation, lines 4739–4820. Agent adaptation to weak poset tuples, positive prism sign, repetitions, and augmentation.

proof.text: The remaining faces have $j=i$ or $j=i+1$. Define $A_i=(f(x_0),\ldots,f(x_{i-1}),g(x_i),\ldots,g(x_n))$ for $0\leq i\leq n+1$, with empty initial or final segments allowed. Then $\partial_iT_i=A_i$ has sign $+1$, and $\partial_{i+1}T_i=A_{i+1}$ has sign $-1$. Their total is $\sum_{i=0}^n([A_i]-[A_{i+1}])=[g(x_0),\ldots,g(x_n)]-[f(x_0),\ldots,f(x_n)]$. Together with the cancellations this gives the desired identity for $n\geq1$.

proof.text: For $n=0$, $H_0[x]=[f(x),g(x)]$, so $d_1H_0[x]=[g(x)]-[f(x)]$ and $H_{-1}d_0=0$. This holds also when $f(x)=g(x)$: the repeated two-tuple is retained in $W_1$ and its boundary is zero. In degree $-1$, $H_{-1}=H_{-2}=0$ and $W(g)_{-1}-W(f)_{-1}=\mathrm{id}_R-\mathrm{id}_R=0$. Below $-1$ the source module is zero. If $P$ is empty all nonnegative source modules vanish. If $Q$ is empty, the existence of $f$ forces $P$ empty. Thus every claimed edge case is included.
